The '''Hans Schneider Prize in Linear Algebra''' is awarded every three years by the [[International Linear Algebra Society]]. It recognizes research, contributions, and achievements at the highest level of [[linear algebra]] and was first awarded in 1993. It may be awarded for an outstanding scientific achievement or for lifetime contributions and may be awarded to more than one recipient. The award honors<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Brualdi|first=Richard A.|date=2015|title=Hans Schneider, 1927–2014|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201511/rnoti-p1380.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=62|issue=11|pages=1380|doi=10.1090/noti1296|doi-access=free}}</ref> [[Hans Schneider (mathematician)|Hans Schneider]], "one of the most influential mathematicians of the 20th Century in the field of linear algebra and matrix analysis.”<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.wisc.edu/hans-schneider|title=Memorial for Hans Schneider {{!}} Department of Mathematics|website=www.math.wisc.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-11-08|archive-date=2015-10-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001094107/https://www.math.wisc.edu/hans-schneider|url-status=dead}}</ref> The prize includes a plaque, certificate and/or a monetary award.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Recognizing excellence in the mathematical sciences : an international compilation of awards, prizes, and recipients|date=1997|publisher=JAI Press|others=Jaguszewski, Janice M.|isbn=0762302356|location=Greenwich, Conn.|oclc=37513025}}</ref>
